observation.visible_scene: A high-angle view of a serpentine line of multicolored dominoes (pink, yellow, teal, white, gray) laid out on a plain concrete floor, with a fixed "Mr.J 01" watermark in the top-left corner. A chain-reaction toppling is already in progress in the upper part of the layout when the excerpt begins; the middle and lower runs and the far-right gray tail are still standing.
visible_changes: At t=0 the leftmost gray/pink tail and the white-base section of the upper loop are already knocked over, with several teal pieces caught mid-tilt, while the middle horizontal row, the lower horizontal row, and the right gray run remain fully upright.
The upper loop finishes collapsing: the teal pieces resting on the white base fall flat, then the pink dominoes on the right side of that loop lean and topple (roughly frames 9–14).

The collapse front passes around the yellow curve at the lower-right of the upper loop and then travels leftward along the upper-middle horizontal row (roughly frames 15–33), tipping over the upright pink/yellow/teal dominoes and the horizontal teal 'bridge' pieces as it goes.
The front reaches the left-hand pink/teal curve of the middle row (roughly frames 30–36) and turns downward into the lower horizontal row.
The lower row then collapses from left to right (roughly frames 36–41); by the last frame the front is around the left-center of that row.

The far-right gray run and the right end of the lower row stay standing throughout; the floor texture and the watermark do not shift relative to the dominoes, indicating the camera is fixed rather than panning.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initially triggered the already-ongoing collapse in the upper loop.
Whether the still-standing middle-right, lower-right, and far-right gray sections ever fall after the excerpt ends.
The final resting state of the layout.
uncertain_details: The exact frame at which each horizontal teal bridge piece drops versus merely being occluded by neighbors.
Whether the camera is perfectly static; the uniform concrete background gives no parallax cue, so very slight motion cannot be excluded, though no relative displacement is evident.
